subject: Astronomy & Space
title: The Building Blocks of Life
description: Learn The Building Blocks of Life in one minute.

hook.text: The ingredients for life are everywhere in space. Carbon, water, and amino acids float in cosmic clouds and comets.

buildup.text: Amino acids—the building blocks of proteins—have been found in meteorites, comets, and interstellar gas clouds.

discovery.text: The Murchison meteorite, which fell in Australia in 1969, contained over 90 different amino acids—many not found on Earth.

twist.text: Having ingredients doesn't mean life will form. The leap from chemistry to biology remains one of science's deepest mysteries.

climax.text: If life's ingredients are everywhere, the question shifts: is life a cosmic inevitability or a rare accident?

punchline.text: Amino acids in meteorites and comets. Life's recipe is scattered across the cosmos.

quiz.question: What did scientists find in the Murchison meteorite?
options: Over 90 different amino acids, including many not found naturally on Earth
Living microorganisms that survived the journey through space
Water ice from a comet that formed in the early solar system

details.summary: The building blocks of life — amino acids, sugars, lipids, and nucleotides — have been found in meteorites, comets, and interstellar clouds. These organic molecules form through natural chemistry in space, suggesting the ingredients for life are scattered throughout the universe.
details.whyItMatters: Finding life's building blocks everywhere in space means the chemistry needed for biology isn't unique to Earth. The universe is pre-loaded with ingredients, dramatically increasing the probability of life elsewhere.
takeaways: Amino acids and sugars have been found in meteorites
Organic molecules form naturally in interstellar space
Life's ingredients are scattered throughout the universe

faq.question: Which meteorite proved amino acids exist in space?
faq.answer: The Murchison meteorite, which fell in Australia in 1969, contained over 90 different amino acids — far more than the 20 used by Earth life. This proved that complex organic chemistry occurs naturally in space without biological processes.

faq.question: Are the building blocks of life the same everywhere?
faq.answer: The same basic organic molecules appear in meteorites, comets, and interstellar clouds, suggesting universal chemistry. However, alien life might use different combinations. Earth life uses 20 amino acids from hundreds of possibilities.
